summary.headline: J&K Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose about 29% QoQ to INR546 crore; management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 14%+ and sees ROA of about 1.20%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR546 crore, up about 29% QoQ with double-digit YoY growth, after a weak Q1. Operating profit rose 27% YoY to INR789 crore, helped by operating expenses up only 2% QoQ and cost-to-income falling to 56.57%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.23% and NNPA at 0.51%, and H1 gross slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier. Management revised FY27 guidance after the mid-term review: credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20% and GNPA below 2%. Key open items are the ECL transition impact, which management will quantify in December, and NIM, which management declined to quantify.

financial_highlights.change: RoA +20 bps QoQ; RoE +250 bps QoQ
Gross slippage amount roughly halved YoY

segments.name: Retail, Agri and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: Entire net incremental credit in Q2 came from RAM; RAM contributed over 60% of YTD net incremental credit. Agri advances grew about 17% YoY and 7.62% QoQ; retail advances grew 3.90% QoQ.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Auto loans grew over 25% YoY; Rest of India housing grew double digits YoY. Retail yield about 10%. Management says 60% of FY27 growth target will come from retail.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri yield about 9.5%. Agri advances grew double digits in H1.

segments.name: Corporate / MSME
segments.commentary: MSME yield about 9%; Rest of India corporate yield about 7.2%. Little large corporate lending in J&K. Management targets 40% of FY27 growth from corporate.

segments.name: Government MoU personal loans
segments.commentary: Outstanding about INR13,400 crore on the MoU personal loan book (management cited INR16,000 crore+ across two variants). Declined last year after product revamp and EMI/salary-ratio correction; H1 FY27 disbursals already exceed full FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revised guidance (after mid-term review): credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20%, GNPA below 2%.
Management says it is 'conservative'; it aims for around 18% credit growth if retail momentum continues.
Management expects H2 FY27 ROA of about 1.40% or better, driven by recoveries from written-off accounts, a special OTS scheme, treasury, fee income and non-fund-based business.
NIM expected to improve substantially from Q3 as the 25 bps repo cut passes through, high-cost deposits are shed, and the repo rate may rise further. No numerical NIM guidance given.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters, returning to current levels in FY28 after hiring.
Credit cost expected to stay around INR70-85 crore per quarter; ECL transition impact to be quantified by December board/next quarter. Management says the ECL hit will be below the industry average.
Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
About 65% of loans are repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked; repo changes passed through the same day.
capex_capacity: Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions; approval already in place, team says it is ready) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
Capital position at 30 Sep 2026: CRAR 16.57%, CET1 13.88%; RoA 1.07% and RoE 13.68% for Q2.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters due to retirements; new hiring to be completed by end of Q3 or early Q4 FY27, taking cost back to current levels in FY28.
Two life insurance partners added (SBI Life, HDFC Life) to expand third-party product sales; management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission reductions.
Retail is the growth focus; management targets 60% of FY27 credit growth from retail and 40% from corporate, with about 18% credit growth aimed for if retail momentum continues.
demand_pricing: Retail and RAM led growth; management says retail is preferred for its higher yield.

Term deposit growth continues to outpace CASA, in line with industry trend. Deposit growth YTD about 7% against 10% guidance (now 12%+ for year). CASA inflows turned positive in Q2 after a sharp Q1 outflow.
Q1 CASA outflows were largely converted to term deposits within the bank, according to management; average and period-end balances are now close.
High-cost CDs of about 8% were taken in Q1 to fund loan commitments; most has been repaid. Remaining high-cost bulk deposits are under INR3,000 crore.
Non-fund-based business up about 30-40% QoQ. Two more life insurers added (SBI Life, HDFC Life); management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission cuts.
Government and salary-account MoUs: more than 20 organisations signed in the last quarter; a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU is expected to be signed the day after the call.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to improve the CASA mix, which lags term deposit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited salary-account MoUs with 20+ organisations, tighter monitoring of UPI POS and QR merchant routing, and a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU. It says CASA is at least held at around 42%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook, and what is the ongoing cost after ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the ECL impact until the end of next quarter, with the model going to the December board. It sees no reason for credit cost to rise; current provisions are ageing-based and H1 slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ROA guidance lowered to about 1.2%, and is H2 ROA of 1.4% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative and the guidance is '1.20 plus', not a downgrade. It expects H2 ROA of about 1.40%, and possibly better, supported by written-off account recoveries and an OTS scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 credit growth of 14% realistic versus 24-25% currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14% is a conservative floor ('14% plus'), with an aim of around 18%. It does not expect 25%, since Q3 and Q4 of last year were strong comparators.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM outlook and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical NIM target but said it will rise substantially from Q3. Drivers are the 25 bps repo pass-through, the end of high-cost deposits, higher yields, and possible further rate hikes. About 65% of the book is repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off treasury gain, and how much was recovered from TWO accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: TWO recoveries were INR25 crore in the quarter. A post-quarter equity stake sale and revaluation gain of about INR100 crore is not in Q2. AFS reserve movement was negative INR62 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL transition hit quantified, and how prepared is the bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL hit will be below the industry average and the bank holds about INR300 crore of buffer. The model is nearly ready and will go to the board in December, when the transitional range will be given.

risks_watch: ECL transition impact is not yet quantified; the range is due in December and the model goes to the board then. Analysts flagged high SMA-0/1/2 (about 5% SMA-1+2).
FY28 ROA sustainability depends on recoveries from written-off accounts and the OTS scheme; management has not quantified these.
NIM improvement is not quantified; cost of deposits rose to 4.85% and yield on advances is flat at 8.55%.
Insurance commission will fall under new IRDAI rules; management expects volume growth to offset this.
Equity raise (INR1,000 crore) timing is open; debt raise (INR500 crore) is expected this quarter.
Q1 CASA outflow has not been fully reversed; CASA ratio is 41.97% against a 42%+ target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the direction of NIM and other income, but guarded on numbers: no NIM figure and no ECL quantum. Management pushed back on the ROA-downgrade framing and called the 14% credit growth guide conservative.
key_quotes: I am 100% sure the NIM is going to go up. I'm not predicting a number, but it is going to go up substantially.
It is not a one-off factor. It is going to continue.
I will give that range in the month of December. I'll give you exact number.

growth.why: FY27 credit growth guided at 14%+ (management says ~18% possible if retail momentum holds), backed by Q2 RAM-led growth, 23.7% YoY advances growth, and partnerships (two life insurers, government MoUs) rather than new capacity; no capacity additions or order book were cited.
